name: Wyoming
modelName: Income shares, combined net monthly income tables written as base amount plus marginal percentage per band (W.S. 20-2-304(a))
incomeDefinition: Income is any payment in money or in kind regardless of source (wages, salary, commissions, contractor pay, workers' compensation, unemployment, disability, annuity and retirement benefits), less reasonable unreimbursed business expenses; overtime counts only if expected to continue on a consistent basis based on the last 24 months; means-tested benefits (Pell grants, POWER, SNAP, SSI) are excluded; potential income is used for voluntarily unemployed or underemployed parents (W.S. 20-2-303(a)(ii)). Net income is income less personal income taxes, social security deductions, the cost of dependent health care coverage for all dependent children, payments under preexisting support orders for other children, other court-ordered support being paid and mandatory pension deductions (W.S. 20-2-303(a)(iii)).

schedule.columns: bands per number of children (1-4, 5 or more): from, percentage of income at band start, base support, marginal percentage over band start
schedule.lookupRule: Combined net income is used in the first column to find the line; the total obligation is the base support plus the marginal percentage of income over the line's amount, then divided between the parents in proportion to net income (W.S. 20-2-304(a)).

belowMin.rule: The tables start at $1,000.00 of combined net monthly income; the statute gives no line below $1,000. The obligor is protected by the self-support reserve of W.S. 20-2-304(f).

formula.text: Total obligation = base + marginal% x (combined net monthly income - band start), from the table for the number of children (W.S. 20-2-304(a)). The obligor's share is the total times obligor net income / combined net income. If obligor net income minus the self-support reserve (current HHS poverty guideline for one person) is less than that share, support is set at that difference (W.S. 20-2-304(f)).

selfSupportReserve.definition: current poverty line for one person, HHS poverty guidelines (42 U.S.C. 9902(2)) (W.S. 20-2-304(f))

shared.text: When each parent keeps the children overnight for more than 25% of the year and both contribute substantially to expenses, the total obligation is multiplied by 150%, divided by income shares, each share is multiplied by the percentage of time the children spend with the other parent, and the parent owing more pays the difference (W.S. 20-2-304(c)). Split custody: the shared amount from the tables is divided per child, allocated by the children each parent has, multiplied by the other parent's income percentage and offset (W.S. 20-2-304(d)).

addOns.childcare: Not added by formula: the cost of necessary child day care is a deviation factor (W.S. 20-2-307(b)(ii)).
addOns.healthInsurance: The cost of dependent health care coverage for all dependent children is deducted from the paying parent's income in computing net income (W.S. 20-2-303(a)(iii)); availability of health, dental and vision insurance is a deviation factor (W.S. 20-2-307(b)(viii)).
addOns.text: Wyoming has no add-on lines in the statute: child care is a deviation factor (W.S. 20-2-307(b)) and dependent health coverage is a deduction from income (W.S. 20-2-303(a)(iii)).

lowIncome.rule: If obligor net income minus the self-support reserve is less than the table amount, support is set at that difference; the reserve is the current HHS poverty line for one person (W.S. 20-2-304(f)). The 2026 HHS guideline for one person in the 48 contiguous states is $15,960 per year ($1,330 per month).

emancipation.text: Support runs to the age of majority (18) and continues for a child between the age of majority and 20 who attends high school or an equivalent program full time, or a disabled child incapable of self-support (W.S. 20-2-303(a)(i), 14-2-204(a)).

testCases.source: Computed by hand from W.S. 20-2-304(a)(ii): combined $6,000, band $4,500: $1,454.00 + 17.0% x $1,500 = $1,709.00; parent A share 4000/6000 = 2/3; $1,709.00 x 2/3 = $1,139.33. SSR check: 4,000 - 1,330 = 2,670 > 1,139.33, no adjustment. https://wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/title20.pdf

facts.text: Wyoming's tables are written in the statute as a base amount plus a marginal percentage per income band, with no income cap: above $15,000 a month a fixed percentage of the excess keeps applying (W.S. 20-2-304(a)).
The self-support reserve is indexed: it is the current federal poverty guideline for one person (W.S. 20-2-304(f)).

If part of the obligor's social security or veteran's benefit is paid directly to the child's custodian, the whole benefit counts as the obligor's income and the amount paid to the custodian is subtracted from the obligor's share, down to zero (W.S. 20-2-304(e)).
The Department of Family Services must review the presumptive child support at least every four years (W.S. 20-2-306); the 2021 review noted the current tables are based on 2012 price levels.
A party who refuses the presumptive amount and loses can be ordered to pay the other party's reasonable attorney fees and costs (W.S. 20-2-307(c)).

uncertain: Effective date of the current tables not found in the compiled statute PDF (no history notes); the 2021 review says the tables are based on 2012 price levels and were not updated in 2016. effective set to null.

Self-support reserve value $1,330/month is derived from the 2026 HHS poverty guideline ($15,960/yr, aspe.hhs.gov) as W.S. 20-2-304(f) directs; the date from which DFS/courts apply each new guideline was not found.

The brief mentioned 40% / 146 nights for shared custody; the statute's threshold is more than 25% of the year for each parent (thresholdOvernights 92 = 25% of 365 rounded up, as 'more than 25%' means at least 92 nights).
No rule in the statute for combined net income below $1,000; no statutory minimum order.
Test case computed by hand from the statute, not from the DFS calculator (calculation is server-side).
